newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says capital controls temporary.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says capital controls temporary.

text.p: Thailand said on Wednesday that current capital control measures introduced by the authorities to curb speculation in the baht were temporary, but more permenant ones would be announced soon.

"They (the controls) are temporary measures. We are trying to plug loopholes for any irregularities that would drain the baht out for speculative purposes," Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan told reporters when asked about the status of the measures introduced since mid-May.
He did not give details on the more permenant measures planned or when they would be announced.
"These (current) measures will lead to more permanent measures which could be introduced soon, but don't ask me when," he said.
The Thai central bank in moves to punish foreign speculators who attacked the baht in mid-May cut off baht supplies to them from local sources.

The move created an informal two-tier baht market -- onshore and offshore -- with foreign players having to scramble and pay a high premium to get much-needed baht supplies to cover their short positions.

On Tuesday, in an unexpected move, the Bank of Thailand moved to plug another loophole for non-resident foreigners trying to raise baht in the stock market. It asked bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid securities sought by foreign investors. It added that non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must pay only in foreign currencies.

Amnuay said foreign and local stocks investors who traded in good faith would not be affected. "What we don't want to see in the stock market is short selling. We want the trading to reflect the real situation," he added.
Brokers said foreigners trying to raise baht funds since last week were actively selling stocks, some of them being short sales, on the Thai bourse.
Commenting on the wide spread between the offshore and the onshore baht values given the current two-tier market, Amnuay said Thailand genuinely did not want such a wide differential.
"It is not our intention to see such a difference in the baht in the offshore and onshore markets, where the baht offshore is much dearer than the one onshore," he said.

"But I would think this reflects temporary irregularities and the current abnormal situation. I believe that it will be temporary and that the values would return to normal when the situation normalises," he added.
Foreign analysts said they were waiting to see when the controls launched by Thai authorities would end as it has made life hard for foreign baht players.
While some have criticised the controls, others say that Thailand has the sovereign right to take certain measures to protect its currency from unnecessary speculative attacks.
